Rents

ACS 5-year 2020–2024, table B25031: median gross rent by unit size, per census tract. Topcoded at $3,501.

These are paid rents, not asking rents. Across the mapped tracts the market asks 1.56× the paid median (Zillow ZORI, 2026-09), so a tract showing $2,400 here is asking about $3,744. The gap is widest where turnover is high and rent control holds the sitting stock down.

Asking rents

Zillow Observed Rent Index, 2026-09, published per ZIP code and allocated to tracts by area-weighting the ZIP Code Tabulation Area overlaps (TIGERweb 2024 boundaries, areas measured in UTM 18N). 90% of mapped tracts fall in a ZCTA that carries an index; the rest are left unpainted rather than extrapolated. ZORI is a constant-quality index of what is advertised, not a survey of what this tract actually pays, and a tract straddling several ZIPs is a blend (the detail card names how many). Ratios built on an ACS margin of error above 30% are drawn faded (345 tracts).

Commute

Transit times are a GTFS graph built from MTA, LIRR, Metro-North and PATH timetables. Bike and walk times come from the OpenStreetMap street network (Valhalla), computed for the 3,274 tracts within 30 km of Penn 1. A tract with no routed time stays unshaded under those modes — nothing is inferred.

Buildings, trees, streets

Buildings are extruded live from OpenFreeMap's OpenMapTiles vector tiles, which carry modelled heights; nothing is downloaded per building. Street trees are the 2015 NYC Street Tree Census (every 4th of 683,788, for payload size). Streets are re-drawn over the 3D mass so the grid stays legible. Buildings are deliberately 42% opaque — solid enough to read as a city, translucent enough to keep the tract colour underneath.

Geometry

Census tracts from TIGER/Line 2024, coast-clipped against TIGER water polygons and simplified as a coverage at 15 m, so neighbouring tracts keep identical edges. Tracts that are ≥ 90% water are dropped.
